title: hybrid stream-to-batch embeddings import with checkpointed retries
creator: Priya Nair
description:
Problem:
Customers hit two pain points when importing large embedding corpora: 1) high tail latency and failed uploads when clients try to stream millions of rows in a single connection, and 2) complex client-side retry logic to achieve idempotent, exactly-once ingestion across partial failures. Existing streaming ingest endpoints were fragile under bursty uploads and didn’t play well with our batch indexing pipeline for reranking workloads.

Goal:
Design and implement a hybrid streaming-to-batch ingestion flow that: (a) lets clients stream rows for low-latency confirmation, (b) checkpoints streamed data into durable chunked objects, (c) processes chunks via async batch jobs that produce final indexed vectors, and (d) provides simple idempotency primitives so clients can safely retry without duplication. Target: scale sustained ingest to 10M vectors/day per tenant with p99 success and reduce client-side retry complexity.

High-level design:
- Client-facing API: /v1/embeddings/import-stream (bidirectional streaming or chunked POST). Clients may supply an optional idempotency_key per top-level import.
- Ingest gateway: accepts incoming rows and writes append-only chunked files to object store (S3/GCS) in per-tenant, per-job prefixes. Each chunk receives a server-generated chunk_id and a sequence range.
- Checkpointing: every N rows (configurable, default 10k) we write a checkpoint manifest with chunk metadata and a SHA256 digest of concatenated row ids to detect duplicates across retries. Manifest is the single source of truth for a job.
- Async job orchestrator: a new job type "embed-chunk-processor" reads manifests and schedules GPU workers to compute embeddings in bulk, using efficient batching and KV cache reuse where applicable. Job writes tokens/embeddings to vector store via an idempotent upsert API keyed by (tenant_id, user_id, row_id).
- Exactly-once semantics: dedupe at write time using upsert with conditional checks on last_processed_chunk_id + digest. A lightweight dedupe table (tenant_id, job_id, chunk_id, digest, status) ensures replays are recognized and skipped.
- Retry semantics: client retries using the same idempotency_key. Gateway will return job_id and upload cursor. Retries append to the same job prefix; duplicates detected via row_id digest. Server side supports exponential backoff and inline status endpoints (/v1/embeddings/imports/{job_id}).
- Flow control/backpressure: gateway uses per-tenant in-memory token bucket with soft throttling and a configurable max inflight chunks. When token bucket exhausted, respond with 429 and Retry-After.

Implementation notes and trade-offs:
- Chunk size: larger chunk size improves GPU throughput but increases restart cost. We picked 10k default, tuned in perf runs to balance latency and throughput (see benchmarks).
- Dedup table vs content-addressed store: dedupe table is lighter and supports TTL-based cleanup; content-addressed dedupe would be stronger but requires sweeping infrastructure.
- Consistency model: eventual consistency for index visibility. We will expose "indexed_count" in job status; final state is only reached after all chunks processed and post-processing compaction job runs.

Acceptance criteria:
- API: clients can create import jobs with idempotency_key and resume an interrupted upload with the same key (server returns stable job_id).
- Correctness: no duplicated vectors observed when the same stream is submitted 3x concurrently with identical content (end-to-end integration test).
- Performance: sustained throughput >= 8k vectors / minute per GPU worker; system-wide per-tenant throughput target 10M/day achievable via autoscale.
- Observability: Console shows per-job progress, p50/p90/p99 processing latency per-chunk, and a triage dashboard for failed chunks with error reasons.
- Rollout: Canary for 5 tenants with >= 99.9% ingestion success during 3-day canary before wider rollout.

Rollout plan:
1) Alpha: internal-only deployment to staging with feature flag; run import jobs from synthetic corpus (1M rows) and collect performance telemetry. (Owned by Alex Wu)
2) Canary: enable for 5 low-risk tenants; monitor ingest success, duplicate rate, and GPU utilization for 72 hours. (Owned by SRE and PM)
3) Broad: opt-in for all self-serve tenants; increase autoscale limits and expose settings in Console.

SDK/API changes:
- SDK: new client helper Embeddings.importStream(apiKey, idempotencyKey, rowsIterable) with automatic checkpointing and resume helpers.
- API contract: minimal breaking changes; we add optional headers and return stable job_id and checkpoint cursor. Docs: https://docs.redwood.ai/embeddings/imports (draft)

Monitoring and metrics:
- New metrics: import_jobs_total, import_chunks_processed, import_chunk_processing_time_seconds_bucket, import_duplicates_detected_total, import_retries_total, import_throttled_requests_total.
- Dashboards: per-tenant import job list, chunk error heatmap, dedupe table size, and average time from upload completion to index visibility.

Security & compliance:
- Uploaded row payloads may contain PII. We ensure objects are encrypted at rest and access-controlled by tenant IAM. Retention policy for intermediate chunks defaults to 30 days and can be shortened.

Open implementation tasks:
- Gateway support for HTTP chunked POST + streaming gRPC endpoint (ENG-A1).
- Dedup table schema and migration plan (ENG-A2).
- Chunk processor job implementation with efficient batching and KV cache reuse (ENG-A3).
- SDK helpers and example notebooks (ENG-A4).
- Console UI for job tracking and manual retry/cancel (ENG-A5).

acceptance_criteria: Clients can create an import job with idempotency_key and receive a stable job_id.
Resuming an upload with the same idempotency_key should not create duplicate vectors (integration test: 3x replay).
System can sustain equivalent throughput to 10M vectors/day per tenant with autoscaling enabled.
Console shows per-job progress, chunk errors, and dedupe metrics for all canary tenants.
Canary run (5 tenants, 72 hours) shows <0.01% duplicate rate and >=99.9% chunk success rate.
